title: Claude Agent SDK [Full Workshop] — Thariq Shihipar, Anthropic
talk_summary: Anthropic's Thariq Shihipar walks through the Claude Agent SDK, arguing that bash plus a file system is the most powerful agent harness (composable, low context, self-verifying) versus many bespoke tools. He frames agent loops as gather-context → act → verify, and stresses deterministic verification, sub-agents for context isolation, and reading transcripts to iterate.

takeaways.technique: Offload tool outputs to files, return paths
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of dumping long tool results into the context window, save results to the file system and return only the path so the agent can grep/re-read and recheck its work.

takeaways.technique: Deterministic verification hooks before LLM review
takeaways.what_they_do: Insert rule-based checks (e.g. error if agent writes a file it hasn't read) as hooks that fire on events and feed errors back to the model, rather than relying only on model judgment.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if the agent tries to write to a file that we know it hasn't read yet... we throw it an error... that's an example of sort of like a deterministic tool that we insert into the verification step

takeaways.what_they_do: Spawn sub-agents for search/verification work so their intermediate steps don't pollute the main agent's context; only the final result returns to the parent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: sub agents are great for when you need to do a lot of work and return an answer to the main agent... there's a bunch of things that don't need to go into the context of the main agent
you probably wouldn't want to like fork the context. You'd probably want to start a new context session and just be like, 'Hey, yeah, adversarially check'

takeaways.technique: Bash + CLI scripts over many bespoke tools
takeaways.what_they_do: Prefer composable bash/CLI scripts (with --help for discovery) and a shared file system over dozens of structured tools, which bloat context and confuse the model.

takeaways.technique: Read transcripts to iterate the loop
takeaways.what_they_do: Treat reading agent run transcripts as the primary design method: inspect what the agent did and why, then adjust prompts/tools/verification accordingly.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the number one thing that the meta learning for designing an agent loop to me is just to read the transcripts over and over again
